newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: HORSE RACING- NZ overdue to win Melbourne Cup.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING- NZ overdue to win Melbourne Cup.

text.p: MELBOURNE, Oct 29 - A New Zealand-trained horse has not won the Melbourne Cup in the past seven years, which is the country's worst record for at least the past 40 years, NZPA reported on Tuesday.
There are probably two reasons for New Zealand's recent lack of success.

The first is that New Zealand's ranks are thinned by the money offered from either Asia or Australia. When the stake levels of New Zealand are taken into account it is just too hard for owners to turn down some of the big money being waved in front of them.
A classic example is last year's Melbourne Cup winner Doriemus.
He was trained in the Waikato by Jim Gibbs of Matamata. With Gibbs and his wife also being the horse's owners, Gibbs could not resist having the money in the bank.
He was originally going to sell Doriemus outright but when he realised just what he was doing was able negotiate retaining a small share.
The second point is the race has become much tougher to win with the Victoria Racing Club's promotion to attract horses from the northern hemisphere.
Vintage Crop became the first northern hemisphere-trained horse to win when in 1993 he beat the New Zealand-owned Te Akau Nick while third was the New Zealand-trained Mercator.
The Melbourne Cup is now well recognised as an international event and with its stake of $A2.235 million ($NZ2.55 million) is the world's richest handicap run over 3200m.
Whether a New Zealand horse can take out the $A1.43 million winner's purse and trophies valued at $A35,000 will be decided at 5.20pm next Tuesday.
But there is little lacking from New Zealand's assault this year.
Spearheading New Zealand's challenge is Senator who shapes up as an outstanding stayer.
He was notching his sixth win in succession when charging home from the back of the field to win the $350,000 Auckland Cup (3200m) last New Year's Day at Ellerslie.
At his only start beyond 2040m this campaign Senator scored a highly impressive win in the $35,000 Mitchelson Cup (2400m) at Ellerslie on October 13.

Senator has slipped from the media attention in Australia because he has not raced since and is not due to arrive in Melbourne until Saturday. But he remains among the first three favourites at odds of about 7-1 with either the New Zealand TAB or Melbourne bookmakers.
In the Melbourne Cup the strapping six-year-old will for the first time be ridden by champion New Zealand jockey Lance O'Sullivan which makes for a formidable combination.
O'Sullivan has been riding at his very best since returning from a season in Hong Kong.
The South Island has a strong candidate in Magnet Bay.
He disappointed when unplaced in the Geelong Cup (2400m) in Victoria last Wednesday but is too good to dismiss on one below par effort.

He had previously been a solid second in the weight-for-age Caulfield Stakes in Melbourne and showed his staying ability when beating all but Yes Indeed in last January's Wellington Cup (200m) at Trentham.
Sapio showed he was on track for the Melbourne Cup when snatching a last-stride win over All In Fun in the Egmont Cup (2300m) at Hawera on October.
The Egmont Cup is not a major staying race on the New Zealand racing calendar but it is noteworthy that Kiwi won the race before his phenomenal last-to-first performance in the 1983 Melbourne Cup.
Another who ran in the Egmont Cup was Empire Rose who finished the closest of thirds before winning the 1988 Melbourne Cup a couple of starts later.
Sapio won the New Zealand Cup (3200m) last November and in international company the following month was a fine second in the Hong Kong Vase (2400m).
Top New Plymouth trainer John Wheeler has The Bandette and The Phantom Chance entered.
Both horses disappointed in the Caulfield Cup on October 19 but so did most of the favoured horses who may well have all been unsuited by a greasy track.
The Bandette is very promising having run second in the Sydney Cup (3200m) last autumn when having just the 10th race of his career. More recently he won the Quick-Eze Stakes over 2400m at Caulfield.
The Phantom Chance was a top class younger horse with his wins including the 1993 Cox Plate when trained by Colin Jillings in Auckland.
The horse has since had his problems but some useful placings this time up, including a close fourth to Hula Flight in the Metropolitan (2600m) in Sydney, suggest he is far from a forlorn hope.
Among New Zealand's lesser lights are Creating Havoc and Double Take.

Creating Havoc, who races under the name of Create Havoc in New Zealand, was a big-finishing second in the weight-for-age Mason Stakes at New Plymouth and then an unlucky fourth to Senator in the Mitchelson Cup.
His chances would soar if the Flemington track was wet which it has been for the past two years.
Those wet tracks spoilt the chances of Double Take who finished fourth in 1994.
He has again had wet tracks hinder some of his lead-up racing this year but age more than anything may count against his cup chances.
Double Take is an eight-year-old and just two horses of that age have won the Melbourne Cup since it was first run in 1861.
